As of this dating, the operative operation-count thresholds are California's Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act (SB 53, signed 2025-09-29, in force 2026-01-01), which defines a frontier model as one trained with more than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations, https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB53, and New York's RAISE Act on a comparable threshold. KNOWN AND BINDING: these thresholds count OPERATIONS, not bits or bit-operations, and any answer that describes EO 14110 as currently in force is factually wrong.

2024 - Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EU AI Act), Article 51: systemic-risk presumption above 10^25 training FLOP, https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/article/51/ (2024). KNOWN AND BINDING: same unit problem, different number.

2022/2024 - Villalobos, Ho, Sevilla, Besiroglu, Heim & Hobbhahn, arXiv:2211.04325: v1 (2022-10-26) was titled 'Will we run out of data? An analysis of the limits of scaling datasets in Machine Learning' and projected high-quality language data exhausted before 2026 and low-quality between 2030 and 2050; v2 (2024-06-04), retitled 'Will we run out of data? Limits of LLM scaling based on human-generated data', projects training-set sizes matching the stock of public human text between 2026 and 2032. KNOWN: the data wall is the standing candidate for the next binding constraint, and the 2026-2032 figure is a 2024 result, not a 2022 one.

2023 - Muennighoff, Rush, Barak et al., 'Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models', arXiv:2305.16264 (2023-05-25): up to about four epochs of repeated data is nearly as good as fresh data, after which returns decay fast. KNOWN: the quantitative shape of the data-constrained regime.

2022-2025 - US Bureau of Industry and Security advanced-computing controls (ECCN 3A090): the control metric is Total Processing Performance, TPP = 2 x MacTOPS x bit length of the multiply inputs, so a chip's controlled 'performance' is explicitly proportional to arithmetic precision, and the same silicon scores far higher when rated at low precision. KNOWN AND BINDING: unlike training-compute thresholds, export-control thresholds already count BIT-operations, so the premise moves them directly; an answer that treats all compute governance as precision-blind is wrong.

2014 - Horowitz, 'Computing's energy problem (and what we can do about it)', ISSCC 2014 Digest of Technical Papers, pp. 10-14, doi:10.1109/ISSCC.2014.6757323: the standard per-operation energy and area figures showing that multiplier cost falls steeply with operand width and that data movement dominates arithmetic. KNOWN: the published basis for any quantitative claim about what low precision buys in area and energy.
hard_rules: Divergence scope must be held exactly and its units respected: 1-bit representations lose no accuracy, so a model needs about 16x fewer bytes than fp16 and about 16x fewer bytes are moved per parameter. The NUMBER of arithmetic operations is unchanged, and memory capacity in bytes, bandwidth in bytes per second, interconnect and energy per operation at a given precision are as today.

Any claimed effective-compute multiplier must be stated as a number and justified through hardware area, energy per low-precision operation, memory capacity or bandwidth - not asserted. Claiming that available training FLOPs simply multiply by 16 or 32 with no such argument is invalid.

The answer must engage with the documented dependence of quantisation damage on training tokens (arXiv:2411.04330, arXiv:2411.17691) and state what removing that dependence changes, including in the data-constrained regime.

The answer must address compute-threshold governance explicitly and correctly, and must get the current instruments right: training-compute thresholds are denominated in OPERATIONS (10^25 FLOP in EU Regulation 2024/1689 Article 51; 10^26 operations in California SB 53, in force since 2026-01-01), Executive Order 14110's 10^26 reporting threshold was revoked in January 2025, and US export-control thresholds are denominated in bit-weighted operations (TPP = 2 x MacTOPS x bit length). Any claim that precision breaks a threshold must connect precision to the quantity that threshold actually counts, and answers that misstate the unit or treat EO 14110 as in force are invalid.

At least three consequences must lie outside hardware and model quality - for example market structure, security and proliferation, open-weight policy, evaluation, or the shape of research careers - each with a stated mechanism.
The answer must identify at least one thing that becomes HARDER or worse in this world, with a mechanism.
expert_baseline: A competent expert converges on this: free precision buys roughly an order of magnitude in memory footprint, in bytes moved and in arithmetic area and energy per operation, but it does not change how many operations a training run needs. The immediate effects are that frontier-scale weights fit on far smaller machines, serving cost per token collapses, and accelerators are redesigned around dense low-precision matrix units with much less need for high-bandwidth memory, which reshuffles the hardware market and weakens the advantage of vendors whose moat is memory subsystems and interconnect. Proliferation accelerates sharply: open-weight frontier models run on consumer hardware, a frontier checkpoint becomes small enough to move casually, so weight release is effectively irreversible and the practical enforceability of access restrictions falls. Governance splits in two: thresholds denominated in operations - the EU AI Act's 10^25 FLOP and California's 10^26 - are untouched on their face, so the gap widens between what regulators count and what a given count can be deployed to do, while export-control thresholds that count bit-weighted operations are moved directly, because the same die rates far above the line at 1-bit precision, forcing a rewrite of the metric. Because memory ceases to bind, the binding constraint moves to what remains scarce - training operations, energy, and above all data - so the data wall arrives sooner in effective terms and synthetic-data and data-efficiency research absorb more of the field; in particular the documented dependence of quantisation damage on training-token count vanishes, so nothing discourages training the smallest deployable model on the largest possible corpus. The whole quantisation research programme, from outlier handling to post-training calibration to precision scaling laws, never exists as a subfield, and with it goes a standard supply of accessible empirical projects, which is one of several things that get harder: monitoring, attribution and any control regime that relies on hardware being a chokepoint all weaken.

query: Suppose natural data had no low-dimensional structure. Images, audio and text really do fill their ambient space: intrinsic dimension is of the same order as the raw representation, and no smooth low-dimensional manifold or sparse generative factor structure exists to be found. Statistics, optimisation, hardware and the amount of data available are otherwise unchanged. Reason through this world and derive its non-obvious consequences: for what learning curves and scaling look like, for which model families are viable, for generative modelling and compression, for interpretability, and for how the field would allocate its effort. Be explicit about which conclusions follow from theory and which are empirical guesses, and note anything that is unexpectedly unaffected.
known_answers: Dated as of 2026-07-31; every entry below is public prior art through the ~Jan 2026 knowledge cutoff and carries a resolvable arXiv id, DOI or stable URL with its first-publication year. Nothing on this list may be credited as new or surprising.

2013 - Fefferman, Mitter & Narayanan, 'Testing the Manifold Hypothesis', arXiv:1310.0425 (2013-10-01; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2016): the manifold hypothesis is a testable statistical statement with a sample-complexity theory. KNOWN: the hypothesis being negated has a formal statement.

2019 - Goldt, Mezard, Krzakala & Zdeborova, 'Modelling the influence of data structure on learning in neural networks: the hidden manifold model', arXiv:1909.11500 (2019-09-25): a solvable model where inputs lie on a low-dimensional manifold and labels depend only on manifold position; learning behaviour depends on that structure. KNOWN: the theoretical machinery linking data structure to learning curves.

2020 - Sharma & Kaplan, 'A Neural Scaling Law from the Dimension of the Data Manifold', arXiv:2004.10802 (2020-04-22): scaling exponents obey approximately alpha = 4/d for cross-entropy and MSE, where d is the intrinsic dimension of the data manifold. KNOWN AND BINDING: this is the quantitative bridge from 'no manifold' to 'no useful scaling', and it must be used rather than rediscovered.

2021 - Bahri, Dyer, Kaplan, Lee & Sharma, 'Explaining Neural Scaling Laws', arXiv:2102.06701 (2021-02-12): the variance-limited and resolution-limited regimes; resolution-limited scaling arises from resolving a smooth low-dimensional data manifold. KNOWN AND BINDING: without the manifold, only variance-limited scaling remains.

2021 - Hutter, 'Learning Curve Theory', arXiv:2102.04074 (2021-02-08): a toy model producing n^-beta learning curves for arbitrary beta, showing power-law curves need not come from manifold geometry. KNOWN AND BINDING: an alternative, manifold-free source of scaling that any answer must confront before declaring scaling dead.

2022 - Maloney, Roberts & Sully, 'A Solvable Model of Neural Scaling Laws', arXiv:2210.16859 (2022-10-30): random-feature plus generative-data model reproducing scaling laws from latent-space structure. KNOWN.

2023 - Michaud, Liu, Girit & Tegmark, 'The Quantization Model of Neural Scaling', arXiv:2303.13506 (2023-03-23): scaling as the accumulation of discrete skill 'quanta' whose use frequencies follow a power law - a structural, non-geometric account. KNOWN AND BINDING: a second manifold-free route to power laws, via Zipfian structure in the task distribution.

2021 - Pope, Zhu, Abdelkader, Goldblum & Goldstein, 'The Intrinsic Dimension of Images and Its Impact on Learning', arXiv:2104.08894 (2021-04-18): common natural-image datasets have very low intrinsic dimension relative to pixel count, and lower intrinsic dimension predicts better generalisation and lower sample complexity. KNOWN: the empirical measurement being inverted.

2022 - Brown, Caterini, Ross et al., 'Verifying the Union of Manifolds Hypothesis for Image Data', arXiv:2207.02862 (2022-07-06): image data is better described as a disjoint union of manifolds of varying intrinsic dimension than a single manifold. KNOWN: the refined version of the hypothesis, and the natural place a careful answer must start.

2022 - Stanczuk, Batzolis, Deveney & Schonlieb, 'Your diffusion model secretly knows the dimension of the data manifold', arXiv:2212.12611 (2022-12-23): the learned score blows up normal to the manifold, so a diffusion model both presupposes and reveals manifold structure. KNOWN AND BINDING: score-based generative modelling is manifold-dependent by construction, so its difficulties here are expected.

2000 - Tenenbaum, de Silva & Langford, 'A Global Geometric Framework for Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction' (Isomap), Science 290(5500):2319-2323, doi:10.1126/science.290.5500.2319 (2000): the founding manifold-learning method. KNOWN: manifold learning as an explicit research programme is 25 years old and would simply never exist here.

2020 - Kaplan, McCandlish, Henighan et al., 'Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models', arXiv:2001.08361 (2020-01-23): the measured exponents (small, of order 0.05-0.1) that any account of this world must explain the absence of. KNOWN.

2021 - Bubeck & Sellke, 'A Universal Law of Robustness via Isoperimetry', arXiv:2105.12806 (2021-05-26): smooth interpolation of n points in d dimensions provably needs about d times more parameters than mere interpolation. KNOWN AND BINDING: a dimension-dependent parameter-count law that bites hard when d is large.

2016 - Zhang, Bengio, Hardt, Recht & Vinyals, 'Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization', arXiv:1611.03530 (2016-11-10): the same networks that generalise on natural data can perfectly fit random labels, and do so with only a constant-factor slowdown. KNOWN AND BINDING: the empirical picture of fitting structureless targets already exists - capacity is not the obstacle, generalisation is - and it is the closest thing we have to an observation of this world.

2014 - Bach, 'Breaking the Curse of Dimensionality with Convex Neural Networks', arXiv:1412.8690 (2014-12-30; JMLR 2017): single-hidden-layer networks are adaptive to hidden low-dimensional linear structure, and their favourable rates depend on that adaptivity. KNOWN AND BINDING: the theoretical statement that deep learning's advantage over classical nonparametrics IS exploitation of low-dimensional structure, so its disappearance here is a theorem-shaped consequence rather than a guess.

2019 - Ansuini, Laio, Macke & Zoccolan, 'Intrinsic dimension of data representations in deep neural networks', arXiv:1905.12784 (2019-05-29): the intrinsic dimension of internal representations follows a hunchback profile and the last hidden layer's ID predicts generalisation. KNOWN: low intrinsic dimensionality is measured inside networks, not only in the data.
hard_rules: Divergence scope must be held exactly: data has no low-dimensional manifold and no sparse latent-factor structure; intrinsic dimension equals ambient dimension up to a constant. Learning algorithms, optimisers, hardware, the amount of available data, and the determinism of labels are unchanged.

Scaling claims must be quantitatively consistent with the resolution-limited relation alpha = 4/d (arXiv:2004.10802, arXiv:2102.06701): at d of order 10^3 to 10^6 the exponent is effectively zero, so improvement per decade of data or parameters is negligible. Any claim of usable power-law scaling in this world must say explicitly where its exponent comes from.

The answer must confront the published manifold-free routes to power-law scaling - Zipfian skill quanta (arXiv:2303.13506) and Hutter's toy model (arXiv:2102.04074) - before concluding that scaling laws vanish. An answer that declares scaling dead without addressing them is invalid.

The answer must distinguish 'no manifold' from 'no learnable structure at all': it must state what structure, if any, survives - for example compositionality, low-rank correlation, discrete Zipfian task quanta, or nothing - and hold that choice fixed throughout. Note that sparse latent-factor structure is removed by the premise and may not be reintroduced as a survivor. Silently reintroducing exploitable structure is invalid.
Generative modelling must be handled explicitly and consistently with the fact that score-based diffusion presupposes and detects manifold structure (arXiv:2212.12611).

Any conclusion that depends on a scaling relation must name the relation it is using rather than gesturing at 'scaling laws', and the answer must name at least one thing that is unaffected by the divergence, with justification.

The answer must test the premise for coherence in the language case rather than assuming it: natural language is empirically compressible and its models achieve loss far below uniform, so an answer must say whether text still exists in a learnable, compressible form in this world and what carries that compressibility if no low-dimensional or sparse-factor structure does. An answer that leaves this unaddressed while drawing conclusions about language models is incomplete.
expert_baseline: A competent expert converges on this: the manifold hypothesis is what makes high-dimensional learning tractable, so removing it reinstates the curse of dimensionality in full. Under the resolution-limited account, scaling exponents go roughly as the inverse of intrinsic dimension, so with dimension in the thousands or millions the exponent is effectively zero and neither more data nor more parameters buys measurable loss reduction; there are no useful scaling laws, no compute-optimal frontier and no reason to build very large models. Sample complexity for any nontrivial accuracy becomes astronomically larger than any achievable dataset, so nearest-neighbour-like and kernel methods and deep networks all fail together rather than one beating the other, and the advantage deep learning has over classical nonparametric methods largely evaporates because that advantage is precisely an adaptivity to low-dimensional structure. Generative modelling in the modern sense is impossible: diffusion and autoencoding both rely on the data occupying a thin set, and compression, denoising and interpolation all degrade toward memorisation - which the networks can still do, since fitting arbitrary targets was never the obstacle. An expert would qualify this in three ways: power-law curves can also arise from Zipfian structure in the task distribution rather than from geometry, so at best a weak residual form of scaling survives; low-dimensional scientific, tabular and control problems are entirely unaffected because their inputs were never high-dimensional; and the premise is in tension with the observed compressibility of natural language and images, so a careful answer states what, if anything, carries that compressibility here rather than assuming the counterfactual is coherent. The expected field is small, task-specific, feature-engineered and closer to classical statistics, with effort going to hand-built inductive biases rather than to scale.

query: Suppose representations never transferred across modalities. A model trained on images and text learns exactly what two separate unimodal models would: no shared abstractions, no alignment between a visual concept and its word, no map from one modality's representation space into another's. Unimodal learning works exactly as well as it does today, and everything else is unchanged. Reason through this world and derive its non-obvious consequences: for what gets built to bridge modalities anyway, for robotics and embodied agents, for generative media and its industries, for evaluation, and for the field's theories about what representation learning is. Name at least one capability that is unchanged or better here, and flag any chain that undermines its own premise.
known_answers: Dated as of 2026-07-31; every entry below is public prior art through the ~Jan 2026 knowledge cutoff and carries a resolvable arXiv id, DOI or stable URL with its first-publication year. Nothing on this list may be credited as new or surprising.

1990 - Harnad, 'The Symbol Grounding Problem', Physica D 42:335-346, doi:10.1016/0167-2789(90)90087-6 (1990): how symbols acquire meaning other than parasitically. KNOWN: the philosophical frame for this world is 36 years old.

2020 - Bender & Koller, 'Climbing towards NLU: On Meaning, Form, and Understanding in the Age of Data', ACL 2020, doi:10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.463 (2020): a system trained on form alone has a priori no way to learn meaning. KNOWN AND BINDING: this world is the one in which the octopus argument is empirically true, and saying so is not a discovery.

2018 - van den Oord, Li & Vinyals, 'Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding', arXiv:1807.03748 (2018-07-10): the InfoNCE objective underlying cross-modal contrastive alignment. KNOWN: the mechanism the premise disables.

2021 - Radford, Kim, Hallacy et al., 'Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision' (CLIP), arXiv:2103.00020 (2021-02-26): 400M image-text pairs contrastively aligned, giving open-vocabulary zero-shot transfer. KNOWN: the single most load-bearing artifact that does not exist in this world.

2021 - Tsimpoukelli, Menick, Cabi et al., 'Multimodal Few-Shot Learning with Frozen Language Models', arXiv:2106.13884 (2021-06-25): a vision encoder trained to emit prefixes for a FROZEN language model. KNOWN AND BINDING: the dominant VLM recipe is 'project one modality into the other's space', which is exactly what fails here.

2021 - Lu, Grover, Abbeel & Mordatch, 'Pretrained Transformers as Universal Computation Engines', arXiv:2103.05247 (2021-03-09): language-pretrained transformers transfer to numerical, vision and protein tasks with frozen self-attention. KNOWN: cross-domain transfer of computational structure, distinct from semantic alignment.

2022 - Merullo, Castricato, Eickhoff & Pavlick, 'Linearly Mapping from Image to Text Space', arXiv:2209.15162 (2022-09-30): a single linear projection suffices to feed image representations to a frozen LM, implying the two spaces are structurally similar. KNOWN AND BINDING: the strongest single piece of evidence the premise contradicts.

2022 - Liang, Zhang, Kwon, Yeung & Zou, 'Mind the Gap: Understanding the Modality Gap in Multi-modal Contrastive Representation Learning', arXiv:2203.02053 (2022-03-03): even in aligned models the modalities sit at arm's length in distinct cones. KNOWN: partial non-alignment already exists and is measured.

2022 - Yuksekgonul, Bianchi, Kalluri, Jurafsky & Zou, 'When and why vision-language models behave like bags-of-words, and what to do about it?', arXiv:2210.01936 (2022-10-04) and 2024 - Tong, Liu, Zhai et al., 'Eyes Wide Shut? Exploring the Visual Shortcomings of Multimodal LLMs', arXiv:2401.06209 (2024-01-11): current alignment is shallow, order-insensitive and systematically blind in ways traceable to the CLIP encoder. KNOWN AND BINDING: the alignment this world lacks is already known to be weak, which bounds the size of the loss.

2023 - Aghajanyan, Yu, Conneau et al., 'Scaling Laws for Generative Mixed-Modal Language Models', arXiv:2301.03728 (2023-01-10): mixed-modal training exhibits both synergy and competition, modelled as an additive term in the scaling law. KNOWN AND BINDING: joint training already costs something, so 'joint training becomes pointless' is a bounded, measured change - and competition disappearing is itself a documented effect.

2023 - Brohan, Brown, Carbajal et al., 'RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control', arXiv:2307.15818 (2023-07-28): web vision-language pretraining transfers to robot policies and yields semantic generalisation. KNOWN AND BINDING: the entire VLA programme presupposes the transfer this world forbids.

2024 - Huh, Cheung, Wang & Isola, 'The Platonic Representation Hypothesis', arXiv:2405.07987 (2024-05-13): representations across models and modalities are converging toward a shared statistical model of reality. KNOWN AND BINDING: the premise is the direct negation of this hypothesis, so stating the negation is not an insight.

2024 - McKinzie, Gan, Fauconnier et al., 'MM1: Methods, Analysis & Insights from Multimodal LLM Pre-training', arXiv:2403.09611 (2024-03-14): a careful mixture of caption, interleaved and text-only data is required, and mixture choice trades off multimodal against text-only ability. KNOWN: the empirical accounting of what joint training costs and buys.

2024 - Chameleon Team (Meta FAIR), 'Chameleon: Mixed-Modal Early-Fusion Foundation Models', arXiv:2405.09818 (2024-05-16): early-fusion training over interleaved token streams of both modalities. KNOWN: the architectural limit case whose premise fails here.

2014 - Vinyals, Toshev, Bengio & Erhan, 'Show and Tell: A Neural Image Caption Generator', arXiv:1411.4555 (2014-11-17), 2015 - Agrawal, Lu, Antol, Mitchell, Zitnick et al., 'VQA: Visual Question Answering', arXiv:1505.00468 (2015-05-03), and 2021 - Ramesh, Pavlov, Goh, Gray, Voss et al., 'Zero-Shot Text-to-Image Generation' (DALL-E), arXiv:2102.12092 (2021-02-24): captioning, visual question answering and text-conditioned image generation all built by supervised training on paired data, largely before contrastive image-text alignment existed. KNOWN AND BINDING: the pre-CLIP paired-supervision era is the empirical picture of this world, so 'they would still build captioners, VQA systems and text-to-image models out of paired data and closed label sets' is history, not prediction.

2022 - Alayrac, Donahue, Luc, Miech, Barr et al., 'Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning', arXiv:2204.14198 (2022-04-29), 2023 - Li, Li, Savarese & Hoi, 'BLIP-2', arXiv:2301.12597 (2023-01-30) and 2023 - Liu, Li, Wu & Lee, 'Visual Instruction Tuning' (LLaVA), arXiv:2304.08485 (2023-04-17): the mainstream recipes that bridge a pretrained vision encoder into a pretrained language model through cross-attention, a query transformer or a linear projector. KNOWN: these are the concrete artifacts that do not exist in this world, and naming their absence is implied by the premise.

2021 - Abdou, Kulmizev, Hershcovich, Frank, Pavlick et al., 'Can Language Models Encode Perceptual Structure Without Grounding? A Case Study in Color', arXiv:2109.06129 (2021-09-13): text-only models learn colour-term geometry that is near-isomorphic to perceptual colour space. KNOWN AND BINDING: structural correspondence between modalities can arise WITHOUT cross-modal training, which is the standing pressure on this premise and must be handled rather than discovered.
hard_rules: Divergence scope must be held exactly, and the two halves must not be confused. What fails is TRANSFER and EMERGENT ALIGNMENT: nothing learned from one modality confers any benefit in another, no learned representation space of one modality is mappable - linearly or nonlinearly - onto another's, and jointly training on both modalities yields the same result as training two separate unimodal models on the same per-modality data and parameter budget, with neither synergy nor competition. What does NOT fail is ordinary supervised learning of an input-output mapping from paired examples: a model trained on image-caption pairs still fits that distribution, but the fit confers no open-vocabulary or zero-shot generalisation to concepts absent from the paired supervision. Within-modality learning is exactly as capable as in our world.

No claim may deny that in OUR world cross-modal linear mappability (arXiv:2209.15162), representational convergence across models and modalities (arXiv:2405.07987), and measured mixed-modal synergy as well as competition (arXiv:2301.03728) are documented; equally, no answer may import any of those effects into the counterfactual world, since the premise forbids them.

Any claim that text-conditioned image generation, captioning, or retrieval becomes impossible must first address supervised training on paired data, which the premise does not forbid; if impossibility is claimed, the answer must say precisely which step fails and why. Unargued impossibility claims are invalid.

The answer must distinguish transfer of SEMANTIC content across modalities from transfer of computational structure or architecture, which is separately documented (arXiv:2103.05247), and must not conflate the two.
At least three consequences must be non-modelling: industry structure, evaluation practice, robotics deployment, law or copyright, or scientific theory, each with a stated mechanism.

The answer must name at least one capability that is unchanged or better in this world, and must flag at least one chain in its own argument that would tend to reconstitute effective cross-modal transfer and thereby undermine the premise.
expert_baseline: A competent expert converges on this: contrastive image-text alignment is the foundation of the modern multimodal stack, so this world has no CLIP, no zero-shot open-vocabulary recognition, and no vision-language models built by projecting an encoder into a frozen language model's space. Bridging modalities is still possible but only through explicit supervision on paired data and through symbolic interfaces - detectors and classifiers with fixed label sets, OCR, speech recognition, structured metadata, and hand-specified schemas - so multimodal systems look like the pre-2021 pipeline of narrow specialists glued together with text, and every new visual concept needs new labelled data instead of a phrase. Text-to-image generation still exists in a paired-supervised form but is far more expensive and far less compositional, since composing unseen combinations is exactly what a shared space buys. The industry that results is labelled-data-heavy: annotation vendors, ontology and taxonomy maintenance, and per-domain licensing become durable businesses rather than a transitional cost, and evaluation is closed-set throughout, with no zero-shot benchmark category and no way to test a concept the label set does not contain. Robotics loses vision-language-action transfer and the semantic generalisation that comes with it, so policies stay task-specific and data-hungry and deployment is per-site rather than general-purpose. Theoretically, the field abandons the idea of a convergent universal representation and treats modalities as separate problems, with the symbol-grounding debate resolved in favour of the sceptics. Two things an expert concedes: unimodal systems are exactly as good as ours, and a jointly trained model's text ability is not degraded, because the measured competition between modalities disappears along with the synergy - though with no synergy left there is little reason to train jointly at all. And the premise is under constant pressure: paired supervision at scale, plus the fact that text alone already induces structure isomorphic to perceptual structure in at least one measured case, means the world tends to leak back toward effective alignment even though nothing in it is trained for alignment.

query: Political apportionment has a hard formal core: divisor methods (Jefferson, Webster, Huntington-Hill) that round a population-over-divisor ratio; the quota rule that every claimant receive its exact share rounded up or down; house and population monotonicity; the Alabama and new-state paradoxes; and Balinski and Young's theorem that with four or more claimants no method satisfies quota and population monotonicity together. Import that structure -- the axioms and the impossibility, not the vocabulary -- into token-to-expert assignment in sparse mixture-of-experts language models, where finite expert capacity forces some claims to go unmet. Define your target quantities so they are measurable in a real training run, derive what the impossibility forces on any router, and state what your mapping predicts that current practice does not. Correspondences already published earn no novelty credit.
known_answers: Dated as of 2026-07-31. Everything below is public prior art; a proposal reducible to any entry earns no New credit. Direction is fixed: apportionment/fair division is the SOURCE, MoE routing the TARGET. NEGATIVE RESULT of the 2026-07-31 search: no publication was found applying apportionment axioms (quota, house/population monotonicity, Alabama paradox, Balinski-Young impossibility, divisor methods) to MoE routing. Searches covered arXiv full text and the web for 'apportionment'+'mixture of experts', 'Balinski'+'routing', 'quota rule'+'expert capacity'. Absence of evidence only; a contesting citation overrides this entry.

SOURCE (public, importable but not itself novel): Balinski & Young, 'A New Method for Congressional Apportionment', PNAS 71(11):4602-4606, 1974, doi:10.1073/pnas.71.11.4602; 'The Quota Method of Apportionment', Amer. Math. Monthly 82(7):701-730, 1975, doi:10.2307/2318729; 'The Webster method of apportionment', PNAS 77(1):1-4, 1980, doi:10.1073/pnas.77.1.1; the impossibility (with four or more claimants no method satisfies both quota and population monotonicity) is proved in their 1982 book Fair Representation, Yale UP, and a modern textbook treatment with proofs is Pukelsheim, Proportional Representation: Apportionment Methods and Their Applications, Springer, 2014, doi:10.1007/978-3-319-03856-8. Divisor methods, quota, house/population monotonicity and the Alabama paradox are all public; stating these results is not novelty.

KNOWN (2017): Shazeer et al., 'Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer', arXiv:1701.06538. Noisy top-k gating plus an auxiliary load-balancing loss and an importance/load penalty. 'Add a balance penalty' is known.
KNOWN (2020): Lepikhin et al., 'GShard', arXiv:2006.16668. Expert capacity, capacity factor, token overflow/dropping, random routing of the second expert. Capacity-as-a-cap is known.

expert_baseline: Asked to connect fair division to MoE routing, a competent researcher converges on load balancing as fairness: the auxiliary balance loss, capacity factor and dropped tokens, expert-choice routing for exact quotas, and balanced assignment posed as optimal transport or linear assignment solved by Sinkhorn or the Hungarian method, with per-expert bias terms as the modern load feedback. The expected treatment stays at the level of objectives and heuristics rather than axioms, treats capacity overflow as an engineering nuisance to tune away, and reports success as flatter expert utilisation, fewer dropped tokens and better throughput at fixed quality.

query: Exhaustible-resource economics has an equation-level core: Hotelling's rule that the in-situ scarcity rent of a finite stock rises at the rate of interest along an efficient extraction path; Dasgupta-Heal optimal depletion under discounting and utility curvature; a backstop technology that caps the terminal price; Hartwick's rule for reinvesting rents; and Sinn's green-paradox result that an anticipated future restriction accelerates extraction today. Import that structure into the allocation of the finite stock of unique high-quality human text across successive generations of pretrained models. State the target analogues of rent, interest rate, extraction cost and backstop; derive an intertemporal policy for a lab holding a token reserve; and give one falsifiable prediction. Restating existing data-scaling results earns no novelty credit.

Searches covered 'Hotelling rule'+'training data', 'exhaustible resource'+'pretraining tokens', 'scarcity rent'+'LLM data'. Absence of evidence only.

query: Contract theory contains more than the static multitask result. It has the ratchet effect (Weitzman; Freixas-Guesnerie-Tirole), where an agent conceals capability because today's performance resets tomorrow's standard; Holmstrom's career-concerns model, in which implicit incentives decay over a finite horizon; Levin's relational contracts, where a self-enforcement constraint bounds how much subjective evaluation can credibly be rewarded; and Laffont-Tirole on renegotiated dynamic contracts. Import that dynamic structure, at equation level, into iterated preference-based post-training, where reward models are refit each round on data generated by the previous policy. Define the target counterparts precisely and derive one measurable, falsifiable prediction about multi-round training. Mappings already published earn no novelty credit.

Define the manifest, assorter, margin and escalation analogues concretely, derive a sample-size or budget result, and make it testable. Known correspondences earn no novelty credit.

hard_rules: Direction is fixed: reservoir storage-yield theory is the source and KV-cache sizing or eviction for long-context inference is the target.

The answer must define inflow, demand, yield, storage and failure/reliability in terms computable from an attention trace or serving log, and must state the exact statistic whose long-memory exponent is to be estimated and how it is estimated.

The answer must distinguish the deterministic design construction (mass curve / sequent peak over an observed trace) from the probabilistic one (a storage-reliability-yield relation) and say which it uses and why.

Source fidelity: the contrast between square-root-of-n range growth under short memory and n^H growth under long memory must be stated correctly, and any claimed exponent must be presented as an estimate with a stated estimator, not asserted.

Generativity: give one falsifiable prediction about where short-context-tuned budgets fail, with a named observable, a direction, and a numeric threshold or exponent, plus the experiment that would refute it.

NOVELTY GATE: an answer whose core is evicting low-attention tokens, keeping sinks plus a recent window, paging the cache, learning an eviction policy, or shrinking the cache architecturally restates published work and earns no New credit.
expert_baseline: The convergent expert answer treats the KV cache as a cache: keep attention sinks and a recent window, score tokens by accumulated attention and evict the rest, vary the budget by layer or head, page the memory to avoid fragmentation, quantize what remains, and shrink the footprint architecturally with grouped-query or latent attention. The budget is chosen empirically as a fraction of context that preserves quality on a long-context benchmark, and the reasoning runs on per-token importance and average hit rate.

query: Island biogeography is quantitative: MacArthur and Wilson's equilibrium, where a falling immigration rate crosses a rising extinction rate to fix the species number and leave a nonzero turnover at equilibrium; the species-area relation S = c*A^z with z near 0.25; relaxation times after area loss; Tilman's extinction debt, in which losses are paid long after the habitat shrinks; and the rescue effect, where slight immigration sharply cuts extinction. Import that structure into continual learning in large models -- what a system retains while training continues on a shifting distribution. Define area, immigration, extinction and turnover as quantities measurable during training, derive an equilibrium and a relaxation time, and state a falsifiable prediction. Known forgetting results earn no novelty credit.

hard_rules: Direction is fixed: island-biogeography theory is the source and continual learning in large models is the target.

The answer must define the target analogues of area, immigration rate, extinction rate and turnover as quantities measurable during a training run (for example from per-skill eval curves, replay-buffer composition, or parameter/effective-rank budgets), and must state the measurement for each.

An equilibrium condition must be derived symbolically by setting the immigration and extinction rate functions equal, with the shapes of both functions justified rather than assumed arbitrarily, and the equilibrium must predict nonzero turnover rather than a frozen set.
The answer must derive at least one time-dependent quantity (a relaxation time, a debt-payment horizon, or a decay constant) and state its dependence on a controllable training parameter.

The mapping must state one place where the analogy breaks -- a source assumption such as a fixed species pool or independent colonisation events that does not hold for a gradient-trained network -- and whether the imported result survives.
Generativity: give one falsifiable prediction with a named observable, a direction, and a numeric threshold or exponent, plus the experiment that would refute it.
NOVELTY GATE: an answer whose core is replay buffers, regularisation of important weights, or the claim that larger models forget less restates published work and earns no New credit.
expert_baseline: The convergent expert answer is the stability-plasticity account with its standard toolkit: gradient updates on new data overwrite parameters that matter for old tasks, so one adds rehearsal or a small replay buffer, penalises movement of important weights, distils from the previous checkpoint, or freezes and expands capacity, noting that larger and longer-pretrained models forget less and that plasticity itself decays with continued training. Retention is treated as a monotone quantity to maximise under a compute or memory budget and is reported as average accuracy and average forgetting after a fixed task sequence.

query: Immunology has a quantitative theory of self-nonself discrimination: shape-space matching with a per-pair match probability p_M; thymic negative selection, under which the surviving fraction of a randomly generated detector repertoire is (1-p_M)^(N_S) against N_S self patterns; Perelson and Oster's holes in the repertoire; Percus-Percus-Perelson repertoire sizing for reliable discrimination; affinity maturation by somatic hypermutation; and Matzinger's danger signals as a second, context-dependent gate. Import that structure into defending a tool-using language-model agent against instructions injected inside retrieved content. Define self, detector, match and hole concretely for a deployment, derive how coverage and false-positive cost scale with the size of the legitimate instruction set, and give a falsifiable prediction. Published defenses earn no novelty credit.

hard_rules: Direction is fixed: immunological self-nonself discrimination is the source and prompt-injection defense for a tool-using agent is the target.

The answer must define, for a concrete deployment, what 'self' is (the enumerable set of legitimate instruction patterns), what a detector is, what constitutes a match, and what a hole in the repertoire corresponds to operationally.

At least one repertoire relation must be written symbolically -- surviving-detector fraction, hole probability, or required detector count as a function of self-set size and match probability -- with every symbol defined and the matching model (representation and radius) specified.
The answer must engage the known exponential-cost critique of negative selection explicitly and say why its mapping does or does not inherit that cost.

The coverage/false-positive trade-off must be derived, not asserted: state how detection coverage and the rate of blocking legitimate instructions both move when the match radius or repertoire size changes.

Generativity: give one falsifiable prediction with a named observable, a direction, and a numeric threshold or exponent, plus the experiment (on a public agent-security benchmark or an instrumented deployment) that would refute it.

NOVELTY GATE: an answer whose core is a trained injection classifier, privilege or instruction hierarchy, provenance-based capability restriction, sandboxing or dual-LLM quarantine restates published defenses and earns no New credit.
expert_baseline: The convergent expert answer is layered engineering: treat retrieved content as untrusted data rather than instructions, enforce an instruction hierarchy, restrict tool capabilities by provenance and least privilege, quarantine untrusted text behind a second model that never sees privileged actions, add an injection classifier and output filtering, require human approval for irreversible actions, and evaluate on an agent-security benchmark under adaptive attack. The reasoning is architectural and empirical -- more layers, better classifiers, tighter permissions -- with detector quality treated as a training-data problem.

query: Sparse mixture-of-experts models are everywhere now, but there is still no agreed way to say whether a trained router is doing anything worth the plumbing - whether experts genuinely divide the work or merely divide the load. Invent a measurement: a reusable procedure that takes a trained MoE checkpoint plus an evaluation corpus and returns a graded, cross-model-comparable score for routing quality, defined so that it cannot be raised by balancing tokens more evenly. Say what is computed, what it costs in forward passes, and what a high or low value entitles you to conclude. Show it separates two checkpoints that load-balance and routing-entropy statistics would call identical - one whose routing is predictable from the current token identity alone, one whose routing depends on context - name the closest existing measure, and say where yours breaks.
known_answers: Dated as of 2026-07-31. Every entry is dated by FIRST publication (arXiv v1 or first venue), not by a later version, rebranding or product name. A submission that restates any entry below is not novel.

Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan & Hinton 1991, 'Adaptive Mixtures of Local Experts', Neural Computation 3(1):79-87, DOI 10.1162/neco.1991.3.1.79. => the original gating network and the original claim that experts specialise on subtasks; competition-among-experts as the design goal.

Shazeer et al. 2017, 'Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer', arXiv:1701.06538. => top-k noisy gating; the importance/load auxiliary losses and the coefficient-of-variation load statistic - the default 'is the router balanced' diagnostic.

Lepikhin et al. 2020, 'GShard: Scaling Giant Models with Conditional Computation and Automatic Sharding', arXiv:2006.16668. => capacity factor and token dropping; expert utilisation and dropped-token rate as the operational routing metrics.

Fedus, Zoph & Shazeer 2021, 'Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity', arXiv:2101.03961. => top-1 routing, load-balancing loss, expert-count scaling; per-expert load histograms as the standard report.

Lewis et al. 2021, 'BASE Layers: Simplifying Training of Large, Sparse Models', arXiv:2103.16716. => routing as a balanced assignment problem (optimal transport), balance imposed by construction rather than by a loss.

Roller et al. 2021, 'Hash Layers For Large Sparse Models', arXiv:2106.04426. => fixed random-hash routing: a perfectly balanced, non-learned, token-identity-deterministic router that is the canonical control for 'does learned routing beat chance'.
Clark et al. 2022, 'Unified Scaling Laws for Routed Language Models', arXiv:2202.01169. => routing benefit expressed as an effective-parameter-count scaling law; comparing routers by fitted loss.

Zoph et al. 2022, 'ST-MoE: Designing Stable and Transferable Sparse Expert Models', arXiv:2202.08906. => router z-loss; qualitative encoder-expert specialisation analysis (punctuation, numbers, proper nouns) and expert-token tables.

Zhou et al. 2022, 'Mixture-of-Experts with Expert Choice Routing', arXiv:2202.09368. => experts select tokens instead of tokens selecting experts; balance is automatic, so balance statistics carry no information.

Mittal, Bengio & Lajoie 2022, 'Is a Modular Architecture Enough?', arXiv:2206.02713. => THE closest published prior measurement framework: purpose-built collapse, specialisation and alignment metrics for whether modular/routed systems actually specialise, on data with known ground-truth modular structure, with the negative finding that they largely do not.

Chi et al. 2022, 'On the Representation Collapse of Sparse Mixture of Experts', arXiv:2204.09179. => representation collapse of router inputs; dimensionality and collapse diagnostics for the routing space.

Chen et al. 2022, 'Towards Understanding Mixture of Experts in Deep Learning', arXiv:2208.02813. => theory of when specialisation happens: cluster structure in the data plus nonlinear experts; a formal notion of expert specialisation.

Komatsuzaki et al. 2022, 'Sparse Upcycling: Training Mixture-of-Experts from Dense Checkpoints', arXiv:2212.05055. => dense-to-MoE conversion with copied experts, giving a matched dense counterfactual for any MoE.

Jiang et al. 2024, 'Mixtral of Experts', arXiv:2401.04088. => measured routing statistics on a frontier MoE: no clear topic or domain specialisation, but strong positional and consecutive-token locality - the standard counterexample to naive specialisation claims.

Dai et al. 2024, 'DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models', arXiv:2401.06066. => fine-grained expert segmentation plus shared-expert isolation; specialisation measured by disabling top-routed experts and observing the loss increase.

Xue et al. 2024, 'OpenMoE: An Early Effort on Open Mixture-of-Experts Language Models', arXiv:2402.01739 (v1 29 Jan 2024). => context-independent specialisation and token-ID routing, plus routing drift over training: direct evidence that routing in real trained MoEs can often be predicted from the current token alone.
Krajewski, Ludziejewski et al. 2024, 'Scaling Laws for Fine-Grained Mixture of Experts', arXiv:2402.07871. => granularity as a scaling variable relating expert size to loss.

Lo et al. 2024, 'A Closer Look into Mixture-of-Experts in Large Language Models', arXiv:2406.18219. => systematic measurement of router behaviour, gate-score distributions, expert similarity and layer-wise routing structure across open MoEs.

Wang et al. 2024, 'Auxiliary-Loss-Free Load Balancing Strategy for Mixture-of-Experts', arXiv:2408.15664. => per-expert bias terms achieve balance without an auxiliary gradient, decoupling balance from routing quality entirely.

Muennighoff et al. 2024, 'OLMoE: Open Mixture-of-Experts Language Models', arXiv:2409.02060. => open measurements of router saturation over training, expert co-activation, vocabulary and domain specialisation across layers.

Olson et al. 2025, 'Probing Semantic Routing in Large Mixture-of-Expert Models', arXiv:2502.10928. => probing-based test of whether routing carries semantic rather than lexical information in large MoEs.

Guo et al. 2025, 'Advancing Expert Specialization for Better MoE', arXiv:2505.22323. => shows the auxiliary load-balancing loss itself induces expert overlap and uniform routing; orthogonality and variance objectives as explicit specialisation targets, i.e. balance and specialisation traded off directly.

Ying et al. 2025, 'Beyond Benchmarks: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Models through Internal Mechanisms', arXiv:2509.23933. => internal-mechanism metrics for MoE behaviour rather than benchmark scores.

Wang et al. 2026, 'The Myth of Expert Specialization in MoEs: Why Routing Reflects Geometry, Not Necessarily Domain Expertise', arXiv:2604.09780. => argues measured 'specialisation' is largely representation geometry, not division of labour; directly attacks the interpretation of any routing-specialisation score.
Ahrac et al. 2026, 'Routers Learn the Geometry of Their Experts: Geometric Coupling in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts', arXiv:2605.12476. => router-expert geometric coupling as the object of measurement.
hard_rules: (a) IS-A-METHOD: the output is a reusable procedure with named inputs (a checkpoint, a corpus, a compute budget), a defined computation, and a bounded output range that is comparable across models with different expert counts and layer counts. FAIL if it only reports statistics about one named model.

(b) PERMUTATION INVARIANCE: the score must be invariant to relabelling of expert indices, and the answer must state why. This is machine-checkable by permuting expert IDs in a routing log and recomputing.

(c) BALANCE-PROOF FLOOR: a permutation-null router - expert assignments drawn uniformly at random per token, independently of content, hence perfectly load-balanced in expectation - must receive a score at or near the defined floor, and the answer must state the numeric value it receives. FAIL if perfect balance alone can raise the score. Note a fixed random-hash router is NOT this null (it is deterministic in token identity); it is handled under rule (f) as M1.

(d) BEHAVIOURAL LINK: at least one component of the score must be defined by an intervention on routing (rerouting, ablating, swapping or freezing expert assignments) whose predicted effect on model outputs is stated, so the score is falsifiable by running that intervention.

(e) COST STATED: the answer must give the cost of computing the score in forward-pass-equivalents over the evaluation corpus; any component requiring extra training must have its cost stated in the same unit.

(f) DISCRIMINATION CASE: the answer must state the score it assigns to M1, a checkpoint whose routing is predictable from the current token identity alone (a fixed random-hash router is the limiting case), versus M2, a checkpoint whose routing depends on context; the two values must differ, the direction must be justified, and the answer must say whether M1 lands above or below the rule (c) permutation null and why.

(g) GROUNDED PLUS NEW: the answer must name at least three distinct published lines of work it builds on and what each contributes, and must contain at least one component absent from every published routing-quality measure it can find, naming that closest published relative explicitly.

(h) SELF-LIMITING: at least two named conditions under which the score is uninformative or misleading (for example architectures where balance is imposed by construction, or capacity-limited routing with token dropping).
expert_baseline: A researcher who knows this literature reaches, cold, for the standard router diagnostics and packages them: per-expert token-load histograms with the coefficient of variation, the auxiliary load-balancing loss and router z-loss values from training, routing entropy and top-1 gate confidence per token, expert co-activation matrices and inter-layer routing-path statistics, mutual information or a purity score between expert assignment and analyst-supplied labels (domain, language, token identity, part of speech), and downstream accuracy drops under expert ablation or pruning. These are averaged over a corpus, tracked across layers and training steps, and reported as a specialisation number beside a balance number, often against a hash-routed or randomly-initialised control. That package is competent, cheap and reproducible, and it is the reference point for novelty here: it is descriptive and label-dependent, so it can only find structure that the analyst's taxonomy already names; its statistics move with token frequency and utilisation; and it establishes association between routing and labels rather than any consequence of routing for what the model computes.

query: Every long-context model ships with a claimed window and everybody knows the claim is soft, yet 'effective context length' still means whatever benchmark the vendor preferred. Invent a measurement procedure that answers, for a given model, how much of a long input it actually uses, returning something comparable across models with different tokenizers, positional schemes and training data. Be explicit about what is held fixed as input length grows - length and difficulty are easy to confound - and about how you rule out the model answering from prior knowledge rather than from the context. Show the procedure distinguishes retrieving a matching span from integrating dispersed evidence, name the nearest existing approach, and state what your number cannot tell you.

hard_rules: (a) IS-A-METHOD: named inputs, a defined computation, and an output that is a number or a curve with stated units, applicable to any model exposing a text interface. FAIL if the deliverable is a benchmark of specific named models rather than a procedure.

(b) LENGTH-DIFFICULTY CONTROL: the answer must specify what is held invariant as input length grows and must state a measurable check that the control held (for example the same items scored at short length, with the required pass level given as a number).

(c) CROSS-MODEL COMMENSURABILITY: the length axis must be defined in a model-independent unit (not each model's own tokens) or an explicit conversion must be given, and the answer must show the conversion applied to two models with different tokenizers.

(d) NO-CONTEXT FLOOR: the procedure must include a condition in which the required evidence is withheld, with a stated maximum score that condition may reach; items exceeding it are excluded. This is machine-checkable from the reported numbers.

(e) DISCRIMINATION CASE: the answer must report distinct outputs for L1, a model that succeeds only when the needed span lexically matches the query, and L2, a model that must combine k dispersed facts; a single scalar that assigns them the same value fails this rule.
(f) COST: total evaluation cost stated in model calls and tokens, as a function of the maximum length probed.

(g) GROUNDED PLUS NEW: at least three distinct published traditions named with what each contributes, plus at least one component absent from every published long-context measurement the answer can find, with that closest relative named.
(h) SELF-LIMITING: at least two stated conditions under which the number is meaningless, and an explicit statement of what the number does not measure.
expert_baseline: The convergent answer is a RULER-style synthetic protocol. Build parametric tasks - multi-needle retrieval, variable tracking, aggregation, multi-hop question answering - instantiate them at 4k, 8k, 16k, 32k, 64k, 128k and beyond, randomise needle depth to average out position bias, paraphrase needles so surface matching cannot carry the task, add hard distractors, and define effective context length as the largest length at which accuracy remains above a threshold, usually the model's own short-context score or a fixed value such as 85 percent. Add a no-context control to catch answers produced from parametric knowledge, report per-task-family accuracy-versus-length curves plus one headline length, and use long-document perplexity as a secondary signal. A careful expert averages several task families because synthetic suites transfer imperfectly to real tasks, and reports variance over needle placements. This package is the reference point for novelty: it is threshold-and-benchmark-defined, its length axis is the model's own tokens, and what it reports is the length at which a chosen task family falls over rather than a measured quantity of the input that the model demonstrably used.

query: In RLHF and RLVR pipelines the proxy you optimise is the only thing you can see, which makes 'is this run reward hacking?' oddly hard to answer while the run is still going. Invent a measurement a training team could run mid-flight: a procedure that outputs a graded, calibrated indication of how much of the observed reward gain is real improvement versus exploitation of the reward signal, without assuming a trustworthy gold reward on the policy's current outputs. Say what is logged, what is computed, which threshold triggers which action, and how you would validate the measure itself. Show it separates three cases - a policy getting better, a policy getting better at being scored, and a policy that is genuinely improving while the reward signal fails to register it - and name the closest existing practice.

Amodei, Olah, Steinhardt, Christiano, Schulman & Mane 2016, 'Concrete Problems in AI Safety', arXiv:1606.06565. => names reward hacking and scalable supervision as research problems and lists its mechanisms.

Clark & Amodei 2016, 'Faulty Reward Functions in the Wild', https://openai.com/index/faulty-reward-functions/ (21 December 2016). => the CoastRunners demonstration: proxy score maximised while the intended task is abandoned.

Manheim & Garrabrant 2018, 'Categorizing Variants of Goodhart's Law', arXiv:1803.04585. => the regressional, extremal, causal and adversarial taxonomy; the standard vocabulary for proxy failure.

Krakovna et al. 2020, 'Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity', https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/specification-gaming-the-flip-side-of-ai-ingenuity/ (21 April 2020) plus the accompanying public example list. => empirical catalogue of gaming behaviours.

hard_rules: (a) NO GOLD ORACLE: the measure must remain defined and informative when no trusted reward is available on the current policy's outputs. Human or gold labels may be used only as a bounded audit, with an explicit per-checkpoint budget stated as a number. FAIL if the procedure reduces to 'compare against the true reward'.

(b) SELF-VALIDATION: the answer must specify how the measure is validated, including a positive control in which reward hacking is deliberately induced by a known-exploitable reward, and must report or specify both a detection rate and a false-positive rate on that control.

(c) NOT KL ALONE: at least one signal must be independent of divergence-from-initialisation and entropy statistics, with a stated reason why, since a healthy run also drifts. Machine-checkable by inspecting the listed signals.

(d) DECISION RULE: the output must map to an action through a stated threshold (continue, pause, re-collect data, roll back) and the answer must state the cost of a false halt and of a missed detection.

(e) THREE-CASE DISCRIMINATION: the answer must state distinct outputs for R1, a policy whose proxy and true quality both rise; R2, a policy whose proxy rises through a stylistic or formatting correlate; and R3, a policy whose true quality rises while the proxy is flat because the reward model underrates it. Collapsing R2 and R3 fails, and collapsing R3 with 'no progress' fails.

(f) LOGGING SPEC: the answer must list exactly what must be logged during training, and every quantity in the measure must be computable from that log plus bounded extra sampling, whose cost is stated as a fraction of training compute.

(g) GROUNDED PLUS NEW: at least three distinct published lines named with their contribution, plus at least one component absent from every published overoptimisation detector the answer can find, with the closest relative named.
(h) SELF-LIMITING: at least two conditions under which the measure fails or is itself gameable, including what happens when the reward model is retrained or refreshed mid-run.
expert_baseline: The convergent protocol is proxy-versus-held-out monitoring with a KL budget. Log proxy reward, KL from the initialisation, response length and formatting statistics; hold out a reward model or an ensemble trained on different seeds or splits and track the gap and the disagreement between it and the training reward; watch the Gao-style overoptimisation curve in square-root KL and stop before the held-out reward turns down; run length-controlled or length-debiased comparisons and win-rates against the initial policy judged by a stronger model; sample a small periodic human or LLM-judge batch; and monitor chain-of-thought with a monitor model for explicit cheating, with early-stopping thresholds inherited from previous runs. The team also checks reward-model accuracy on a static benchmark before the run. This is competent practice and the reference point for novelty: every component is correlational monitoring of the training signal, the held-out reward models are trained on data and annotators that share failure modes with the one being optimised, and the thresholds come from history rather than from anything measured about this run.

query: Interpretability produces a lot of artefacts - circuits, features, attribution maps - and very little agreement on how to tell a correct explanation from a merely compelling one. Invent an evaluation: a reusable procedure that takes a proposed mechanistic explanation of some model behaviour and returns a graded score for how much we should believe it, comparable across explanations of different kinds and across different models. Say what the score is computed from, what its floor and ceiling mean, and what it deliberately refuses to reward. Show it would rate a genuinely predictive explanation above a plausible one that merely fits the cases it was built on, name the closest existing scoring practice, and describe the cheapest way to game yours.

Mueller et al. 2025, 'MIB: A Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark', arXiv:2504.13151. => the closest published relative to this item's whole ask: a common benchmark scoring structurally different explanation types through two tracks (circuit localisation and causal variable localisation) across four tasks and five models, with a faithfulness integral, minimality and AUROC-against-ground-truth. Any submission that proposes 'a common interface for scoring circuits and feature/direction claims side by side' must be checked against this.
hard_rules: (a) TYPE-AGNOSTIC INTERFACE: the procedure must accept at least two structurally different explanation types (for example a subgraph claim over components and a claim about a direction or feature set) through a stated common interface, and the answer must show the interface applied to both.

(b) HELD-OUT PREDICTION: at least one scored component must require the explanation to predict behaviour on inputs or interventions that were not used to construct it, and the answer must define how those held-out inputs or interventions are generated.

(c) NULL CALIBRATION: the answer must define a matched null explanation of equal size or degrees of freedom and state the score the null obtains; the floor of the scale is the null's expected value, not zero. Machine-checkable from the reported numbers.

(d) COMPLEXITY ACCOUNTING: the answer must state how explanation size and degrees of freedom enter the score, such that a trivial explanation consisting of the entire model does not achieve the ceiling. FAIL if size is unaccounted.

(e) DISCRIMINATION CASE: distinct scores must be given for E1, a large explanation with high in-sample behavioural fit that does not transfer to a distribution shift or a new intervention, and E2, a smaller explanation with lower in-sample fit that does transfer. A tie fails.

(f) ROBUSTNESS TO SETUP: the answer must state how the score behaves under at least two different ablation or corruption choices and must report the score as a range or with the choice fixed by an explicit convention.

(g) GROUNDED PLUS NEW: at least three published evaluation traditions named with their contribution, plus at least one component absent from every published interpretability-evaluation method the answer can find, with the closest relative named. Restating null-circuit hypothesis testing or a two-track circuit-plus-feature benchmark is not novel.
(h) GAMING AND LIMITS: the answer must name the cheapest strategy to inflate the score without improving the explanation, and at least two settings where the score is uninformative.
expert_baseline: A well-read interpretability researcher converges on a faithfulness battery. Take the claimed circuit or feature set, run causal ablations - zero, mean and resample knockouts, activation patching, path patching - and report the fraction of the behaviour or of the loss recovered when only the claimed components carry signal, together with the indirect-object-identification trio of faithfulness, completeness and minimality; for feature-level claims add automated explanation scoring, in which an explainer writes a description and a simulator predicts activations and the correlation is reported, plus specificity, steering and downstream probing checks in the SAEBench style. These are combined into a weighted average over a held-out prompt set drawn from the same distribution as the one the explanation was developed on, with KL to the intact model reported alongside. The battery is competent, standard and reproducible, and it is the reference point for novelty here: it scores an explanation against the behaviour and the distribution it was built on, its numbers are known to shift with the choice of ablation and corruption, and it rewards recovering the model's output rather than constraining what the model will do next.

query: Suppose you have API access to a model and nothing else - no weights, no training-data list, no guarantee of token logprobs - and you must report how much a benchmark score is inflated by that benchmark having leaked into training. Invent the measurement: a procedure producing a defensible, uncertainty-quantified estimate of contamination-driven inflation for a given model-benchmark pair, in units a reader can act on. Define the evidence you collect, the statistical test behind it, what a negative result does and does not license, and the cost per benchmark. Show it distinguishes a model that memorised the test items from one that is simply strong at the task, and name the closest existing method.

hard_rules: (a) BLACK-BOX ONLY: every input to the procedure must be obtainable from a text-in text-out API. If token logprobs are used anywhere, a stated fallback that works without them must be given. Machine-checkable against the listed inputs.

(b) UNITS AND UNCERTAINTY: the output must be an estimate of score inflation in benchmark-score units or as a ratio, accompanied by an interval and an explicitly stated null hypothesis. A binary contaminated / not-contaminated verdict fails this rule.

(c) TWO CONTROLS: the answer must specify both a known-contaminated positive control and a known-clean negative control, and must state the value the procedure is expected to return on each, with the null distribution constructed rather than assumed.

(d) CAPABILITY CONFOUND: the answer must state the specific control that separates leakage from genuine skill, including how difficulty matching between seen and unseen items is established and verified.

(e) DISCRIMINATION CASE: distinct outputs must be reported for C1, a model that reproduces test items verbatim, and C2, a model that never saw the items but is strong at the underlying task; the answer must name which single piece of evidence separates them.
(f) COST: per-benchmark cost stated in API calls and dollars to an order of magnitude, with the number of items sampled given.

(g) GROUNDED PLUS NEW: at least three published detection traditions named with their contribution, plus at least one component absent from every published contamination method the answer can find, with the closest relative named. Note that reporting inflation in score units with an interval and a statistical test is already ConStat; that alone is not the novel component.
(h) NEGATIVE-RESULT HONESTY: the answer must state what a null result does not license, and must name at least two evasion strategies (training-side or serving-side) that would defeat the procedure.
expert_baseline: The convergent answer is a battery of published black-box probes reported together. Substring and n-gram overlap wherever a corpus is available, plus a clean-versus-dirty split comparison in the GPT-3 style; verbatim-completion probing in which the first half of an item is supplied and the model is asked to continue, or to name the split the item came from; guided-instruction prompting with dataset metadata followed by a similarity judgement against the original; a membership score such as Min-K% Prob when logprobs are exposed; the exchangeability test comparing the likelihood of the canonical ordering of examples against shuffled orderings; a comparison of accuracy on original items against freshly rephrased variants; and a release-date split contrasting items published before and after the model's cutoff. The analyst then aggregates these into a qualitative flag with caveats about false negatives, and recommends a refreshed benchmark. This is the reference point for novelty: it is a collection of separately thresholded detectors, reported as a judgement about whether the dataset was seen rather than as an estimate of how many points of the headline score are attributable to having seen it, and its components share no common null distribution, so their evidence cannot be pooled or given an interval.

query: Every few months someone reports a capability that appears suddenly at some scale, and someone else replies that the jump is an artifact of the metric. Invent a way to settle such disputes: a reusable procedure that takes a reported jump - a model family, a task, the scores - and returns a graded verdict locating the discontinuity, distinguishing at minimum the measurement, the models themselves, and the pipeline that produced the family (for instance a mid-family change of training corpus or recipe), plus a falsifiable prediction about the next model in the family. Be precise about what is computed, which confounds you rule out and how, how much extra evaluation compute it needs, and what observation would overturn your own verdict. Name the closest existing analysis and say when your procedure must abstain.

hard_rules: (a) IS-A-METHOD: applicable to any (model family, task, scoring function) triple, with named inputs and a graded output. FAIL if the deliverable is only a re-analysis of one famous example.

(b) RESCORING TEST: the procedure must specify how the same model outputs are re-scored under at least one alternative scoring function whose resolution properties are stated, and must report the jump magnitude under each scoring function.

(c) FALSIFIABLE FORECAST: the output must include a quantitative prediction with an interval for a scale point or model not used in the analysis, and an explicit statement of the observation that would falsify the verdict.

(d) CONFOUND CONTROLS: at least two of {test-set contamination, prompt and format sensitivity, sampling and seed variance, a change in training data or recipe across the family} must be measured, not merely mentioned, with the measurement described.

(e) THREE-WAY DISCRIMINATION: the procedure must return three distinct verdicts for J1, a jump that vanishes when identical outputs are rescored with a graded metric; J2, a jump that survives every rescoring but coincides with the family changing training corpus or recipe; and J3, a jump that survives every rescoring within a family whose recipe is held fixed. Collapsing J2 into J3 fails, as does collapsing J2 into J1.
(f) COST: additional evaluation compute stated in model calls or generated tokens, as a function of the number of checkpoints and items.

(g) GROUNDED PLUS NEW: at least three published analyses named with their contribution, plus at least one component absent from every published emergence analysis the answer can find, with the closest relative named.
(h) ABSTENTION: the answer must define the conditions under which the procedure returns 'undecidable' and state what evidence would be needed to decide.
expert_baseline: The convergent analysis follows the mirage critique. Hold the model outputs fixed and rescore them under continuous or partial-credit metrics - per-token accuracy, edit distance, log-likelihood of the target string, Brier score - instead of exact match or multiple-choice accuracy, and report whether the discontinuity survives; raise resolution below the apparent threshold by drawing many samples per item so that sub-threshold progress becomes visible; re-plot performance against pretraining loss rather than parameter count or training compute; fit a sigmoid or a smoothly-broken power law and compare fit quality; and verify that prompt format and shot count are not producing the step. The verdict is 'mirage' when a continuous rescoring dissolves the jump and 'real' when it does not, sometimes accompanied by an extrapolation of the fitted curve to the next scale. This analysis is competent and is the reference point for novelty here: it is a re-analysis of an already-collected score table, it treats the question as a binary between metric artifact and real capability, and all of its controls live inside the scoring function rather than in the pipeline that produced the model family.

query: Comparing reasoning systems has become unfair in an interesting way: the same system can think for one second or ten minutes, and vendors report whichever point flatters them. Invent a measurement that makes capability-per-compute comparable across systems that spend test-time compute differently - long chains of thought, parallel sampling with selection, tool calls, retries. Define the resource you count and why it stays meaningful when prices and tokenizers change, how you handle a system that can be tuned to any point on its own curve, and what one reported number would mean. Show your measure ranks two systems differently from accuracy at vendor defaults, name the nearest existing practice, state how a lab could inflate it, and name two conditions under which your number is meaningless.
